## Why This Is Asked

This explores runtime policy enforcement in KCNA at scale, focusing on cross-tenant leakage, late data handling, and performance.

- Per-tenant policy store
- Inline policy evaluation
- Row-level masking and retention

## Code Example

```javascript
function evaluatePolicy(ctx, rec){
  const policy = policies.get(ctx.tenant);
  if(!policy.allows(rec)) throw new DenyError();
  return rec.mask(policy.visibilityMask);
}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests cross-region privacy, key management, attestations, and ordering in KCNA at scale; fills coverage gap from existing questions.

## Key Concepts

- Data locality across regions
- Tenant-scoped encryption and KMS attestations
- Monotonic per-tenant sequencing for cross-region ordering
- At-least-once delivery with idempotent stores
- Latency budgets and failure modes

## Code Example

```javascript
// Envelope seal example (pseudocode)
function sealTenant(payload, tenantId, regionKms) {
  const key = regionKms.getKey(tenantId);
  return encrypt(payload, key);
}
```

```
flowchart TD
  Ingest[Ingest Event] --> Encrypt[Encrypt w/ Tenant Key]
  Encrypt --> Route[Route to Region]
  Route --> Deliver[Deliver to Regional Replica]
  Deliver --> Attest[Attestation Verify]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test key rotation without tenant disruption?
- How would you detect and remediate cross-region locality violations?
- What latency budgets and SLOs would you commit to for inter-region replication?
